edges.description: 11p15 ICR1 hypomethylation alters expression of IGF2 in the imprinted fetal-growth region.
Reduced IGF2 growth signaling impairs fetal and childhood growth.
Increased CDKN1C cell-cycle inhibition restricts prenatal and postnatal growth.
Loss of HMGA2 or PLAG1 growth-regulatory function restricts prenatal and postnatal growth.
Parent-of-origin imbalance is associated with reduced growth.
Gestational growth restriction is what produces birth weight or length that is small for gestational age.
Growth restriction continues after birth as postnatal growth failure.

Relative macrocephaly reflects growth restriction of the body with relative sparing of cranial growth; it is defined against the reduced birth weight or length rather than caused by growth restriction alone.

nodes.description: Loss of methylation at 11p15 ICR1, the H19/IGF2 imprinting domain, disrupts an imprinted growth-control region and acts through reduced paternal IGF2 expression. CDKN1C is regulated by the separate IC2/KvDMR1 domain and is not raised by ICR1 loss of methylation; increased CDKN1C activity in SRS belongs to CDKN1C gain-of-function variants and maternal 11p15 duplications (see the CDKN1C Gain-of-Function node).

nodes.description: Rare maternally inherited CDKN1C gain-of-function variants increase activity of the imprinted cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor p57KIP2, increasing cell-cycle inhibition and restricting growth. This is the opposite direction to the CDKN1C loss of function seen in Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome.

evidence.snippet: Silver-Russell Syndrome (SRS) is typically characterized by gestational growth restriction resulting in affected individuals being born small for gestational age, with relative macrocephaly at birth (head circumference ≥1.5 standard deviations [SD] above birth weight and/or length), prominent forehead with frontal bossing, and frequently body asymmetry.
